memory_lessons.applicability: For this stencil, test alias information as a separate aid to compiler auto-vectorization; the measured no-directive versions so far were much slower than the explicit-SIMD candidate.
memory_lessons.claim: Three valid candidates measured 0.081288 s with the compile-gated OpenMP SIMD hint, 0.449431 s with pointer induction and no hint, and 0.461277 s with indexed accesses and no hint. The latter two show that removing the hint alone did not approach the measured hinted result in those trials.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this no-SIMD, restricted-pointer variant for correctness and both core budgets, including setup costs.

proposal.hypothesis: The best measured candidate combines hoisted row bases with OpenMP SIMD (0.081288 s), while two no-directive candidates measured 0.449431 s and 0.461277 s. This experiment removes the SIMD directive but gives GCC/Clang a guarded no-alias guarantee for the coefficient, input, velocity, and output streams. The compiler may then auto-vectorize the contiguous-x loop without a target ISA, alignment, or fixed-width assumption; the ordinary loop still handles all widths and tails.

retained: Removed the compile-gated OpenMP SIMD directive to test compiler auto-vectorization without an explicit SIMD hint.
Added GCC/Clang-guarded restrict qualifiers to the coefficient, stencil input, velocity, and output pointers to expose their non-aliasing relationship without asserting alignment or vector width.
Preserved the recurrence, initialization, boundaries, generic loop bounds, and scalar tail behavior.
